cases.story: Steady business, clean, asking for exactly the Lender tier limit.
cases.why: Clean steady business; $50,000 is exactly the Lender tier ceiling.

cases.story: Steady business, clean, just above the Lender tier limit.
cases.why: Clean steady business; $55,000 needs the Branch Manager.

cases.story: Seasonal business; the off-season still breaks even.
cases.why: Seasonal (55% in peak), off-season roughly breaks even: Northgate structures a seasonal line, Kite offers a standard line, Aspen declines on variability.

cases.story: Strongly seasonal; most months lose money outside the peak.
cases.why: Strongly seasonal, most months negative: Northgate still structures around the peak; Kite's typical month is negative; Aspen declines on variability.

cases.story: Seasonal business asking for a line larger than its peak season can repay.
cases.why: Line requested exceeds what peak season can repay: Northgate approves a smaller seasonal line; Kite a small standard line; Aspen declines.

cases.story: Invoice-based business with very uneven months.
cases.why: Invoice income with very uneven months: Aspen declines on variability; the others approve on cash flow.

cases.story: Invoice-based business with fairly even months.
cases.why: Invoice income with even months: Aspen's policy still requires tax returns for self-employed invoice income, so it refers.

cases.story: Steady business with two bounced payments in the last 90 days.
cases.why: Two NSFs in 90 days: Northgate approves with conditions; Kite and Aspen decline.

cases.story: Steady business with three bounced payments in the last 90 days.
cases.why: Three NSFs in 90 days: declined everywhere.

cases.story: Business spending more than it brings in.
cases.why: Business spends more than it earns: declined everywhere.

cases.story: Large, strong practice financing $400,000 of equipment.
cases.why: Strong practice: approved, $400,000 goes to Northgate's credit committee; Kite approves up to its maximum.

cases.story: Cash business with one single cash deposit of $12,000.
cases.why: Cash deposit of $12,000 is a FINTRAC LCTR candidate (single transaction), never a credit factor.

cases.story: Cash business with two deposits totalling $10,500 within 24 hours, across midnight.
cases.why: Two cash deposits totalling $10,500 within 24 hours across midnight: LCTR candidate under the 24-hour rule.

cases.story: Cash business whose largest day is a $9,900 deposit: just under the reporting threshold.
cases.why: Largest cash deposit $9,900: just under the LCTR threshold, so no flag.

cases.story: New business with nine months of history, otherwise healthy.
cases.why: Nine months of history: under Aspen's 12-month minimum; fine for Kite and Northgate.

cases.story: Growing business whose existing debt leaves little room for a new loan.
cases.why: Existing debt limits the new loan: each lender counter-offers a smaller amount.

cases.story: Clean salaried member with plenty left over each month.
cases.why: Clean salaried file with ample coverage passes every policy.

cases.story: Clean salaried non-member, small loan.
cases.why: Clean file; membership isn't needed for a small installment loan.

cases.story: Three bounced payments in the last 90 days.
cases.why: Three NSFs in 90 days exceeds every lender's limit (CU 2, Kite 1, Aspen 1 per 12 months).

cases.story: One bounced payment in the last 90 days, otherwise clean.
cases.why: One recent NSF: within Kite's limit of 1 and Aspen's 1 per 12 months; Northgate approves but adds NSF conditions.

cases.story: Two bounced payments in the last 90 days.
cases.why: Two NSFs in 90 days: over Kite's 1 and Aspen's 1 per year; within Northgate's 2, so approval with conditions.

cases.story: Two bounced payments seven to nine months ago, none since.
cases.why: Two NSFs 7-9 months ago: outside Kite's and Northgate's 90-day windows, inside Aspen's 12-month window.

cases.story: Thin credit file (5 months), steady pay, Northgate member.
cases.why: Thin file: Northgate's member starter path and Kite's starter cap approve; Aspen needs 24 months of credit history.

cases.story: Thin credit file (5 months), steady pay, not a member.
cases.why: Thin file and not a member: Northgate's starter path needs membership; Kite's starter cap still approves; Aspen declines on history.

cases.story: Thin Canadian file, but an imported foreign credit report is available.
cases.why: An imported foreign credit report substitutes for Canadian history at Aspen and lifts the thin-file caps.

cases.story: Only seven months of account history, long credit file.
cases.why: Seven months of account data: below Aspen's 12-month minimum, above Kite's 3; Northgate has no minimum.

cases.story: Steady gig income from daily payouts.
cases.why: Steady gig income: Kite and Northgate approve on cash flow; Aspen refers for two years of tax returns.

cases.story: Gig income with two bounced payments in the last 90 days.
cases.why: Gig income with two recent NSFs: Kite declines (max 1), Aspen declines (max 1 per year), Northgate approves with conditions.

cases.story: Retiree on a workplace pension, long-time member.
cases.why: Stable pension income and a long membership: approvable everywhere.

cases.story: Credit cards at 95% of their limits and climbing.
cases.why: Card utilization above 90% breaches every lender's maximum.

cases.story: Credit cards at about 85% of their limits, stable.
cases.why: Utilization near 85% is high but under every lender's 90% maximum.

cases.story: Stable pay, but only about $250 a month left over.
cases.why: Low surplus: each lender should counter-offer a smaller amount rather than decline outright.

cases.story: Spends more than they earn every month.
cases.why: Negative monthly cash flow: no lender can support new payments.

cases.story: Existing loan payments take almost everything left over.
cases.why: Existing debt consumes the surplus; even the product minimum isn't affordable.

cases.story: Long-time member whose coverage sits just under the standard minimum.
cases.why: Coverage between Northgate's relationship (1.1x) and standard (1.2x) minimums: approve on relationship, one tier up. Others counter-offer smaller.

cases.story: High earner asking for more than any lender's personal loan maximum.
cases.why: Strong earner asking above product maximums: each lender approves at its own maximum.

resolved.cause: The engine classified invoice-based income by how much it varied, so even invoice income looked like a steady business and skipped Aspen's tax-return referral. Invoice-based describes how income arrives (a few direct client payments a month), not how variable it is.
resolved.fix: Income is now classed as invoice-based when most of it is direct client payments arriving a few times a month. Card-processor settlements got their own transaction category so weekly card batches are not mistaken for invoices. Expectation unchanged.
